subject: Re: PoC deployment mode & trial plan - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmecorp.com>, Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: PoC follow-up - deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private)

Thanks for the time today - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call highlights:
- You want low-latency inference for customer-facing features (sub-200ms median) and predictable unit costs.
- Primary concerns: data residency for EU/US customers, formal SLAs for production, and integration with your internal key management.
- Deployment modes discussed: Hosted API (fastest start), Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput, shared data controls), Private VPC/on-prem (full isolation, required for some regulated workloads).

Recommended PoC approach (high-level):
1) Short trial on Hosted API to validate integration, prompts and quality (2 weeks).
2) Parallel sizing exercise for Dedicated capacity if you need predictable throughput (bench tests + load profile, 1 week).
3) If compliance requires, scope Private VPC customer deployment (security review + provisioning, timeline TBD).

Immediate asks for planning:
- Please confirm the success criteria for the PoC (latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy/quality bar).
- Who are the stakeholders for the PoC (engineering, security, procurement) and their preferred kickoff week?
- Any hard procurement/contract deadlines?

Attached: redwood-poc-outline-acme-v1.pdf (high-level PoC options and responsibilities).

Next steps: If you confirm success criteria + stakeholders, we'll circulate a concrete 3-week PoC/trial plan with milestones, resource commitments (SE time), and what success looks like for each deployment mode.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmecorp.com>

Date: 2026-10-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PoC follow-up - deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private)

Thanks Ben - helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Compliance: For EU customers we need data residency in an EU region and SOC2 evidence. Hosted API is fine for an initial quality test but procurement will push for either Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated GPU pool on Redwood) or Private VPC if we need to guarantee data separation and network control.
- Hard deadlines: Procurement aims to have a contract in place by end of October to align with our Q4 roadmap.
- Success criteria (initial suggestion):
  * Latency: median <= 200ms for 512-token requests
  * Throughput: handle bursts to 50 concurrent requests without >500ms p95
  * Quality: automated evals on our benchmark prompts >95% pass rate
  * Security: SOC2 evidence + KMS integration for key management (or HSM)

Can you provide ballpark pricing for a 30-day Dedicated capacity trial vs a Private VPC baseline? Procurement will need numbers to start internal approvals. Also looping in Javier from security (javier.martinez@acmecorp.com) — he'll want to review the SOC2 artifacts.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Product Lead, Search & Relevance | Acme Corp
emily.zhao@acmecorp.com

Appreciate the detail, Emily - that helps a lot. Quick responses to the asks below: 

- Ballpark pricing: I'll get you a 30-day trial estimate for Dedicated capacity and a baseline for Private VPC by EOD Monday. That will include SE hours for onboarding and load testing. (Pricing note: Dedicated is typically subscription-based for reserved GPU pools; Private VPC has an initial provisioning fee + monthly platform fee.)
- Success criteria: we'll formalize your bullets into measurable checks in the PoC plan (latency/throughput/quality/security).
- Stakeholders: please confirm Javier + procurement contact for the kickoff invite. Also let us know if your infra team needs a technical deep-dive prior to kickoff — Marissa (SE) can run that.

I'll draft the 3-week PoC/trial plan and share it (target: Tue 10/5).

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-05T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: PoC/trial plan + success criteria (draft) - Acme Corp

Hi all - attaching a draft PoC/trial plan based on the call and follow-ups. Highlights below and attachments: redwood-poc-plan-acme-v1.pdf, soc2-evidence.zip, and a short runbook link.

PoC summary (3-week plan)
- Week 0 (prep, 3 days): access & onboarding, share test prompts, set up keys (Hosted API sandbox or Dedicated dev pool).
- Week 1 (integration & quality): integrate SDK, run automated eval suite, identify prompt fixes. Success check: quality eval >= 95% on provided benchmark.
- Week 2 (load & latency): ramp tests to simulate production traffic; measure median latency and p95 under burst. Success checks: median <= 200ms, p95 <= 500ms at target concurrency.
- Week 3 (wrap + recommend): review results, cost analysis, recommended deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC) and estimate for production.

SE commitments:
- I'll allocate three half-days (remote) for onboarding + two full test days for load runs.

Security & compliance:
- Included SOC2 artifact bundle (see soc2-evidence.zip). For KMS/HSM integration we'll provide a technical checklist and sample config for Private VPC or Dedicated.

Attachments / links:
- redwood-poc-plan-acme-v1.pdf (detailed milestones and responsibilities)
- soc2-evidence.zip (SOC2 summary, control owners, sample reports)
- Runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-poc
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-2026-ACME-145

Please review and confirm:
1) Success criteria above (quality/latency/load/security)
2) Which deployment mode you want to exercise first as part of the PoC (we recommend Hosted API for fast validation, plus a parallel sizing run for Dedicated).
3) Preferred kickoff week (we have availability starting week of Oct 18).

If you confirm, I'll book kickoff, calendar invites and SE time.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
